 There are only a few airlines that continue to operate the Airbus A380 , and Qatar Airways is among them. The Doha-based airline and one world member currently operates eight of the double-decker aircraft. According to aviation analytics company Cirium , it has scheduled more than 2,800 A380 flights between November 2026 and September 2027.

 Until the weekend's schedule update, the Qatari flag carrier had planned to deploy the aircraft on four routes from March 2027, when the summer schedule begins. These included flights from Doha Hamad International Airport (DOH) to Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK), Paris Charles De Gaulle Airport (CDG), London Heathrow Airport (LHR), and Singapore Changi Airport (SIN). However, the airline has now removed the A380 from its Singapore schedule. 
 Qatar Airways Drops Planned A380 Flights To Singapore From March 2027
 Credit: Arseniy Shemyakin Photo | Shutterstock 
 Interestingly, Qatar Airways only started deploying the superjumbo on the route earlier this year. Historical schedule data and Flightradar24 records show that it operated its 517-seat quadjet on a handful of flights between DOH and SIN in January and February. In fact, Cirium data indicates that A380 services were also scheduled for March, although flight-tracking records show that the last scheduled flight of the type operated on February 28.
 The airline had initially planned to bring the Airbus double-decker back to Singapore in September, but subsequently moved its return to late March next year, coinciding with the start of the summer schedule. Its previously planned operations for April can be seen below. These flights are now scheduled to operate using it 283-seat Airbus A350-900 , which features 36 business class seats and 247 economy seats.

 The latest filing shows the oneworld alliance member will operate just one A380 flight on the route, scheduled for April 5, 2027. This might change in the future. Overall, Qatar Airways currently offers two to three daily flights between Doha and Singapore, primarily using the A350-900. It also occasionally deploys its larger A350-1000 and Boeing 777-300ER aircraft on the route. 
 London Heathrow Gains More Qatar Airways A380 Flights
 Credit: AV8 Photos | Shutterstock 
 It appears that the Qatari flag carrier may be reallocating some of its A380 capacity to LHR. Before the SIN flights were removed, the airline had scheduled one daily A380 service to the UK airport, but this has now increased to two daily flights. Elsewhere, from November onwards, the airline has scheduled up to 11 weekly A380 flights to BKK and one daily service to CDG, although the latter will not see any quadjet operations in April or May.
 In general, Qatar Airways' A380 deployments have declined compared to last year, based on scheduled operations between January and December 2026 against the same period in 2025. SIN is not the only destination to lose the double-decker . The airline has also stopped deploying the type to Perth International Airport (PER) and Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (SYD), both of which saw regular A380 operations last year.

 In addition, the Gulf giant had planned to return the type on its Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (CAN) route from October 25, but the aircraft has since been removed from the schedule . It will continue to serve the Chinese city using the smaller, 412-seat 777-300ER.

 Five Airlines Will Continue Operating Airbus A380s To Singapore
 Credit: Markus Mainka | Shutterstock 
 Furthermore, even without Qatar Airways' A380 services, SIN will continue to see regular operations by the world's largest passenger aircraft. From November onwards, five airlines are scheduled to operate the type at the airport: British Airways , Emirates , Etihad Airways , Qantas , and Singapore Airlines . 
 The UK airline only returned the superjumbo to Singapore last month . It previously operated the aircraft to the Lion City between 2014 and 2020, and brought it back in 2024. That deployment continued until May 2025. Meanwhile, Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways is scheduled to resume A380 flights to Singapore on December 16.

 In a typical week next summer, Changi Airport is expected to see an average of around 16 daily A380 departures. For obvious reasons, Singapore Airlines will account for half of these, deploying its double-deckers on routes to destinations including Auckland, Delhi, Mumbai, London, Frankfurt, and Sydney.

 El_hancho   Qatar airways 777s especially the ones replacing the A380 routes are neither inconsistent in hard product nor ancient.
 Avio and you are so ignorant and don't know a dime about QR 777 fleet. 
 QR 777s are of two types A7 BE and A7 BA series. A7 BE 100% guaranteed Qsuites while A7 BA have 8 normal 777s but rest are all mostly Qsuites . A7 BE is on an average 9 years old with new IFE in economy while A7 BA is 17 years old with slightly older IFE in economy. 
 The replacement 777 300 ers QR operate to former A380 routes like Sydney and Perth are mostly all A7 BE series which are new 9 year old 777 300ers which means they are SAME AGE AS A380s.
 QR 777s have stuff that QR A380s dont have as listed below.
 1. Starlink 100 Mbps free wifi. A380 is a rickety 10 $ unusable wifi.
 2. Qsuites business class. Better than even A380s old outdated first class lol let alone its outdated reverse herringbone business class.
 3. A 4 way headrest in all QR 777 economy( both old and new). Most QR A380s can only move up and down. No folding. 
 4. 3 pouch seat pocket in all QR 777s ( both old and new). Most A380s only have a single pouch pocket.
 5. Far quicker service in 777 300er than A380 due to smaller size of 777s than A380. 
 6. At least in A7 BE series 777 300er which operates frequently on former A380 routes like Sydney/Perth the IFE was far less laggy than the one I had on A380. 
 Both have similar legroom too. I didnt find any difference at all. The only area where QR A380 beats 777 is slightly wider seats. Frankly though 777 seats are just big enough for me to have decent flight. 
 But in the rest of the areas ??? "Ancient horrible" QR 777 300 er blows the QR A380s out of water. 
 The fact that A380 wifi is paid and unusably bad, while 77w starlink wifi is free , extremely fast and uniform throughout flight is enough for me to judge which Qatar airways aircraft is better.
 If you find 777 noisier ??? Just get a noise cancelling headphone imao. Its 2026 already. 🤣
